Red Light for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel, macOS 11 or newer)

Install: drag Red Light into the Applications folder.

First launch: this build isn't signed or notarized by Apple, so macOS blocks the first open
with "Red Light can't be opened because Apple cannot check it for malicious software" (or
"Apple could not verify Red Light is free of malware").

  macOS 14 and older: in Applications, right-click (or Control-click) Red Light, choose Open,
  then click Open in the dialog.
  macOS 15 and newer: double-click Red Light once and click Done. Then open System Settings >
  Privacy & Security, scroll down to "Red Light was blocked", click Open Anyway, and confirm
  with your password or Touch ID.

macOS remembers the choice; after that Red Light opens normally.

Turn your volume down before the first play: the kick has a lot of low end.

Keys: Space play/stop, Esc stop, A-D or 1-4 pick a pattern slot, Up/Down tempo, Left/Right swing,
Cmd-S save. Click a step to toggle it; click a voice name to hear it. Songs are JSON files in
~/Library/Application Support/Red Light (OPEN > Open folder shows them in Finder).
Red Light 0.1.0 was called Backroom: songs saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Backroom
are copied across on first start, and the old folder is left alone.

Command line: "/Applications/Red Light.app/Contents/MacOS/redlight" --help
(for example --render to write a song to a WAV file without opening the window).

Free and open source: https://github.com/nunyabiz765/redlight
From Center Point Labs: https://centerpointlabs.dev
